The extensive and continuous help of Mr. and Mrs. E. A. McMahon of Dallas deserves particular mention, with Mr. McMahon's being general chairman of the College Reunion Committee made his home a center for the exchange of advice, information, and documents. Through this Committee, headed first by Mr. Guy W. Thomason (who later had to devote his time to the Hamill Memorial Gymnasium project) came my first contact with materials not available through correspondence; and for the prompt and full answers to my questions, thanks again.

Documents, photographs, and souvenirs which depict so realistically the activities of people of the long-existent College came from chests, trunks, and souvenir boxes of many students, and all were contributed with a great deal of care and effort on the part of busy and elderly people. For these invaluable contributions, I am especially grateful to the donors:
